newsitem.title: USA: IMF to visit Ethiopia after loan payment delays.
newsitem.headline: IMF to visit Ethiopia after loan payment delays.

text.p: Experts from the International Monetary Fund visit Ethiopia next month, but several issues have already delayed the release of part of a three-year loan, an international monetary source said on Monday.

The source said a 1997 tranche of a $115 million Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility had been delayed due to IMF concern that Ethiopia was not freeing up its exchange rate and interest rate system quickly enough.
Next month's talks would now center on payments for the 1997-98 financial year, he added.

"Ethiopia is a country which is growing rapidly and where inflation rates are below five percent," the official said. "The issue is whether they are in a strong enough position to liberalize and open up their economy and our view is yes."

Prolonged IMF delays in paying tranches of the loan to Ethiopia could hurt Adis Ababa's ability to win debt relief under the international HIPC initiative, which rewards highly indebted countries with a strong record of economic reforms with large-scale debt relief.

Uganda, a reformist star on a continent where economic growth has long lagged potential, was the first country to win HIPC debt relief. Ethiopia, many of whose debts are to Russia, had been viewed as a candidate.

The official said the IMF was satisfied at Ethoipia's performance on inflation and economic growth, but had asked the authorities to simplify rules on currency remittances, export earnings and interest rate payments.
This would be needed for the country to integrate into the world economy, he said.
